scenarios.name: Small nested UI: 50 nodes
scenarios.question: What does a complete 50-node nested layout transaction cost?
scenarios.description: A deterministic near-balanced hierarchy alternates row and column Flexbox containers. It represents nested application UI while keeping the topology identical for every package and API.
scenarios.transaction: Create the public tree, apply styles, attach every child, calculate layout, read left/top/width/height for every node, and release resources when the API requires it.

scenarios.description: A deterministic near-balanced hierarchy alternates row and column Flexbox containers. It represents nested application UI while keeping the topology identical for every package and API.

scenarios.name: Wide wrapping collection: 500 items
scenarios.question: What does a complete layout transaction cost for one broad wrapping collection?
scenarios.description: A two-level Flexbox collection exercises broad child lists, wrapping, repeated style conversion, child attachment, layout reads, and resource release without random fixture generation.
scenarios.transaction: Create the public root and 500 items, apply styles, attach every item, calculate layout, read left/top/width/height for every node, and release resources when the API requires it.

scenarios.name: Styled node construction: 500 leaves
scenarios.question: What does creating many nodes from one reused multi-field Style cost?
scenarios.description: One Style value carrying fifteen fields is applied to every leaf, so the transaction is dominated by public Style input conversion and node creation rather than by tree shape or layout work.
scenarios.transaction: Create the public root and 500 leaves from one shared Style value, attach every leaf, calculate layout, read left/top/width/height for every node, and release resources when the API requires it.

scenarios.name: Coding-agent chat: initial layout
scenarios.question: What does it cost to build, measure, lay out, read, and release a modeled coding-agent screen?
scenarios.description: A fixed desktop chat fixture contains a session sidebar, measured labels, a message transcript, and a composer. Text callbacks use the same intrinsic-size function and constraints for both public APIs.
scenarios.transaction: Create the public tree from fixed fixture data, calculate with public text-measure callbacks, read left/top/width/height for every node, and release resources when the API requires it.

scenarios.name: Coding-agent chat: viewport resize
scenarios.question: What does it cost to relayout an existing measured application tree after a resize?
scenarios.description: The same coding-agent fixture is created and initially laid out before timing. Each transaction alternates between two fixed viewport sizes, recomputes measured layout, and reads every result.
scenarios.transaction: Update the persistent root size through the public API, calculate layout with public text-measure callbacks, then read left/top/width/height for every node. Setup and final release are outside timing.
